utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Witness, I shall ask you once again, what were you in the process of doing at that moment? Were you carrying out the combat orders at that time?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understand it, on the 17th of April, when I was issued weapons and I was up there fortifying the line, that is, on the 17th of April, I was therefore a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So on the 16th of April, you were a uniformed civilian in Ahmici, but on the 17th of April, you were an armed combatant on the front; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you explain, how is it that you changed the status from one to the other?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Well, I already said it. Slavko Papic came to fetch me. He came sometime in the morning, I don't remember, and told me I was to go up to Pirici. I tried not to, I resisted. I told him that I had this back pain and that I couldn't. But it did not help much at the time, so that I had to go to the area of Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Who is Slavko Papic? Who was Slavko Papic at the time? What was Slavko Papic at the time?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: At that time, Slavko Papic, to me he was kind of a commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But what were his duties? The commander of what?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Well, that I don't know, I don't know. I mean if he came to my place, then it meant -- well, then it should mean that -- I mean at the time there were -- as far as I know, there were some village guards at the time, so that should mean that he perhaps was the one who deployed the elderly to be on guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Couldn't you be more accurate? Couldn't you be more specific and offer us a more understandable explanation? You were not an elderly person, you were not one of the guards, so what happened?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I don't really know what were Slavko's duties, whether he had any responsibilities, and I didn't understand what you meant when you referred to me. What did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I shall ask another question. So you don't know what were the duties and responsibilities of Slavko Papic, but you nevertheless knew that you had to obey him; is that so?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, naturally, because the day before -- yeah, well, I believed I was duty bound. I believed I was duty bound to go up there if I could help, but I couldn't help. I say I wish I had stayed at the centre and been on duty that evening rather than to go out there and then be wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What happened on the eve of that? It was on the eve of that that you were assigned to that task, on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, it wasn't on the 16th. I said I was given it on the 17th, when Slavko Papic came to my place and asked me to go to the area of Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When is it that you were issued a weapon?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: When I got to Pirici, up to Pirici.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Who gave you the weapon?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: I was given the weapon by an elderly man. It was an M-48 rifle, M-48.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: All right. As we have decided, the re-examination shall be deferred until tomorrow morning. Is that so, Mr. Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, although I could continue with -- I think there is no need to delay it until tomorrow, regardless of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I simply forgot to tender this document 369 into evidence. Thank you, Mr. President. (Trial Chamber confers)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Susak, very well. If you are ready to re-examine the witness now, then please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Although I have not talked about this to the witness, I know what the state of the facts is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. Covic, you said that Ivica Semren was wearing what? Was he wearing a military uniform or civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: He was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So he was wearing civilian clothes. What kind of uniform was Drazenko Vidovic wearing?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: He was wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So he was also wearing civilian clothes. Was Slavko Rajkovic wearing civilian clothes or a uniform?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Slavko Rajkovic had a black uniform on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You were talking about the 16th of April, 1993. When was there gunfire in Santici, in the morning or in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When was there gunfire on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Well, it started in the morning at half past 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When did it stop, according to you, since you were outside that day?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Well, it went on the whole day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When did the intense gunfire stop?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Well, sometime around -- well, it was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So according to you, if you say "in the morning", I assume it was before noon that the shooting stopped.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So can you tell me, considering the fact that you said that Slavko Rajkovic was killed and that Ivica Semren, who was a civilian, and Drazenko Vidovic, who was also a civilian, were wounded, were they taking part in some kind of operation or were they attacked from an ambush while there was no shooting?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were attacked from an ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they were not taking part in military operations?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What were they doing? Were they walking, or ... ?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were going on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Ivica Semrin and Drazenko Vidovic, were they being treated for any wounds if they were wounded that day?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that they received medical treatment after they were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you see the corpse of Slavko Rajkovic?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where did you see it?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Well, on the 16th of April, just before dusk, because that was when my neighbours brought him from there, because they had learned that he had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where did he come from, do you know? Where was he born?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. You said that you had bought a camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What would have happened if you hadn't bought it? How would you have gone to your job at the centre for alerting people?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: I would have gone in civilian clothes, just as the other people there did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So were you obliged to wear a military uniform when you were going to your job?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. So if you did not have a uniform, did you have any patch on your camouflage uniform when you went to work?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: No, I personally did not have a patch, but the others who worked there before me, who had worked there for years, had a patch saying that they worked in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that Slavko Papic told you on the 17th of April to go to Pirici, to the defence line?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you consider yourself to have been mobilised on that day?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: On that day? On that day, Slavko sent me to the line of defence, and I took my weapon, so I consider that I was a soldier then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: From then, from the 17th of April, 1993; so you consider that you were mobilised on the 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Since you worked in the monitoring, reporting, informing, and alerting centre, you were active there?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I went there every day, except --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So before the 17th of April, were you ever sent to perform duties toward Vlasic or on Kuber?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were you able-bodied?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't in good health physically, which is why I worked in the monitoring, reporting, informing, and alerting centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So to sum up, you consider that Slavko Rajkovic, Drazenko Vidovic, and Ivica Semrin were attacked from an ambush?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I will ask you, were they on their way to perform a military operation, or were they simply walking?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: They were simply walking. They were not performing an operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know from where someone shot them?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: The gunfire came from -- there is a house, and that's where the shots came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: The Prosecutor suggested that Ivica Semrin was a member of the HVO. Was he a member of the HVO or a civilian on that day?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but he wasn't wearing a camouflage uniform, he was not carrying a rifle, so I think he was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you consider him to have been a civilian?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know whether anyone except you, on the 16th of April, 1993, and -- you, Josip Covic, and the other person, went to Ramiz Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know whether someone else went to Ramiz Ahmic's house, except for you, on the 16th of April, 1993? Did anyone else besides you go to that house?

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: You mean besides me, Josip, and Slavko?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOSIP COVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I'm asking you because other witnesses said that someone else went to that house during the day but before you arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't have any questions for you, Mr. Covic. You may be released. (The witness withdrew) (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Bralo. Would you please make the solemn declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. Counsel Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Bralo. Would you please introduce yourself to the Court with your full name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: My name is Finka Bralo. I was born in 1958. I live in Santici with my husband and my two sons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What is your husband's name?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: My husband's name is Anto Bralo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you please tell us where your house is exactly?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: My house is in Santici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is it close to Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Before I show you the aerial photograph, I will put a few short questions to you. Would you tell us where you were on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 1993, I was at work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And where were you employed?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: In UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you worked in UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When you were working at UNPROFOR, did you have a uniform?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What did the uniform consist of?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: The uniform consisted of trousers, olive green, with two big pockets at the sides, and normal pockets as well, and the top was like -- it was a camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was it camouflage?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 1993, were you at UNPROFOR working?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I was. All day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Can you tell us, your husband, Anto Bralo, where was he employed?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: My husband, Anto Bralo, was also employed in UNPROFOR. We worked together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What did he do there?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: He worked with fuel, a stoker. He worked at night sometimes, depending on the shifts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Could you tell us whether he also had a uniform similar to yours?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: It was the same uniform. The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I will repeat my question: Did he have a uniform issued by UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, issued by UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that you and Anto Bralo were at work on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you please tell us when you went to bed on the 15th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: On the 15th of April, 1993, we went as usual at half past 10.00 or 11.00 p.m. We had to get up early in the morning. We had to go to work, and I had to get up early to feed our livestock before going to work and leave everything in the house in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So we shall now discuss the 16th of April, 1993. When did you wake up in the morning?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: In the morning we were awakened by gunfire, so we got up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What time was it?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: The gunfire started at around half past 5.00, 5.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. So how did you experience this?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, it was very stressful. There was gunfire. We didn't know what to do. We had to go to work. Our children were in the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So had you known that conflict would break out, would you have stayed in your house with your children?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Of course not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you would have left?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And then you say you got up; you were awakened by gunfire at about 5.30?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What did you see then?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I went out onto the balcony. I have an open terrace. And Kata Kovac, my neighbour, was running across the meadow with her husband and her son in the direction of my house. They arrived at my door.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Kata came in with her son, and my husband went outside and invited our neighbour in. They stayed outside on the terrace, talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Would you say what the name was?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Anto Bralo.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And what about the neighbour who came?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Frano Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: They lingered a little at the door, talking, and I brought my neighbour inside to take care of her child, and when I looked out again, they had left the terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: My husband and Frano Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Anto Bralo and Frano Kovac?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And where did they go?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: They set out down the road, and Drago Josipovic was standing on the road, and Anto Papic, and they probably went toward them. But then Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic set out toward the house of Nikola Omazic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: In the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, in the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And where did Anto Bralo and Frano Kovac go?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: They went toward Anto Papic's stable, down the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And Drago and Anto Papic, they just went on?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, they just went on down the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: As you said?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And did Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic take the road in the direction of Nikola Omazic's house and further on?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you see what happened? Did they encounter anyone?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, (redacted), (redacted), with her two children, were going towards them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was there anybody else there?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic met them. They stopped on the road and talked a little, and then they all started going back in the direction of the house of Anto Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So did they go on down the road, or did they come back?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No, they turned back with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was Hasim Ahmic there, as well, among the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I heard that he was, but I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And where did they go then?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: They went to the house of Anto Papic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where were you then, as they were passing down the road?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I was standing on my terrace. I was surprised. I went in and out, but I kept looking through the window. There's a good view from my house, and you can see everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What time was it, approximately, when the family of (redacted) came to Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, it could have been 20 minutes to 6.00 or a quarter to 6.00. Not later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know whether any other Muslims were in Anto Papic's house on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, all our nearest neighbours, all those who lived in our street, they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did they feel safe in Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, most probably, because if they hadn't felt safe, they wouldn't have gone there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: During the day, did you go to Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you tell us why you didn't go?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, the reason was that we did not have much contact. My family did not contact a lot with his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So these were small matters?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You weren't there, but did you hear what other -- which other Muslims were in that house on that day?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I heard that Cazim Ramic, Zilka Ramic, Biba Ramic and her two children, Mirsad Osmancevic, Saiba Osmancevic and her three children. Then there was (redacted) with her two children, her mother, as I heard, but I didn't go there, so I didn't see them, but I heard that they were there. There was (redacted) (redacted), and her two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You already mentioned them; very well. Did any of the Muslims come to your house from Anto Papic's house on that day?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, her husband, Asim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And how long did they stay? Did they sit down?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Hasim stayed with my husband in front of the door, in the courtyard, and his wife came and wept.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: His wife went in and wept?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes. She didn't want to sit down on the couch. She sat down next to her -- she wept. I wept with her, and she said, "Dear Finka, they've killed my Fahran." So what else could we do but weep? So she sat on the floor. I gave her a glass of juice. She drank it, and then she sat for a while, and then she left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were the Muslims able to go in and out of Anto Papic's house as they wished?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Of course. Nobody stopped them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you see them going out?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did they walk up and down the road?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mentioned Mirsad Osmancevic; would you tell us who he is?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Who Mirsad is?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. Who is he?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Mirsad was my neighbour. Mirsad was a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He often went somewhere. I don't know where, he didn't tell us, but we later heard that he was a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He would stay away from home for some 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So did you all know that he was a member of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, we all knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And that he went somewhere?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know where he went?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, I think -- no, I'm sure that it was Preocica. The place was called Preocica where he went.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was that a training centre for the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know whether on that same day Mirsad Osmancevic was in Rovna?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Mirsad was in Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And his family?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, and his children.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How old was his youngest child? Was it older or younger than a year old?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, it was about a year old.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I will now ask you about the layout of Anto Papic's house and the living conditions there.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: The layout in Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Well, if you didn't go there -- when was the last time you went there, or did you hear people describe it, or what did it look like from the outside?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, I had been to his house before, because we contacted before we stopped. And the layout, to tell you, is very bad. It's poor. There is one room which is both a living room, a bedroom, and a kitchen, and there's a narrow hall.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were some Croats in his house, besides Muslims?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: If you do, can you tell us which of the Croats were there?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Ljubica Papic, Ruza Papic, Andjelina Papic, Marko Papic, and Anto Papic himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And Anto Papic's wife, was her health all right?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And his sister is a young person, or old?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: She is an old woman.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is Anto Papic's wife alive today?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And when did she die?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I don't know. I think it was after the war. After the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: After the war, you are saying; could Mirsad Osmancevic, with his small child and other children, could he live in the conditions such as prevailed in Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is that the reason why he went in the direction of Rovna?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I think so. I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know, who did he go in Rovna to?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I do. He went to Jozo Cerkez's.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And Jozo Cerkez is a Croat, is he?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, he is a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How long did they stay there, if you know that, if you heard it from someone?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I did not hear from anyone how long they stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And did you hear that they had come back?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I did hear that they came back, because Mirsad Osmanac --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Osmanac, or Osmancevic?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No, he is Osmancevic, but we called him Osmanac for short. He asked my husband to go and bring him over from Rovna. My husband wasn't home. He had gone, because Marija Papic had asked him to go to her stable with Frano Kovac and feed the livestock, because she had two cows, and so one had to feed those cows and milk those cows. So she wasn't at home when Mirsad called. In the meantime, when my husband came, I told him that he had been looking for him, and he went to Anto Papic's house. Mirsad had already come back from Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did Mirsad come to Anto Papic's house, come back to Anto Papic's house, with his whole family?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And when he came back, did somebody threaten him? Were you also afraid?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, naturally, of course I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were you afraid?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I have only two more questions. In the morning, when you saw Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic, did you see what Drago Josipovic was wearing?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I did. Drago was wearing civilian clothes, and he had an army vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was it a flak jacket?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: It was a camouflage vest.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And Anto Papic?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Anto Papic wore military clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now let us move on to the 17th of April, '93. Did you see Drago Josipovic that day?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes. Drago Josipovic, he came to my place, where we had coffee around 9.00 in the morning together with Frano Kovac and Katica Kovac. They were at my place, having coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How long did he stay there?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, he could have been an hour and a half, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where did he go then?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Drago told us he was going home to feed the livestock. He was going home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Whose home?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: His own home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did he go there?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: In the direction of his home?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: In the direction of his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That day, did you see the Muslims when they left Anto Papic's house and started for the road; did you see them?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But did you hear that they had left?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Which one of the Croats went with them?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Anto Papic went with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did somebody else go with them except Anto Papic; did you hear anything?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No, no. Nobody else, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, when they started in the direction of the road, did you see Anto Papic after that?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, shortly afterwards. Shortly afterwards, Anto Papic came and we could see them all day long, and he came also into my yard and asked me and my neighbour, Kata Kovac, he asked us if we could give something for [indiscernible] child, for the baby, because the baby was an infant and needed milk and some sugar and some clothes, and we tried to put something together and put it in a bag, and gave it to Anto Papic to take it with him. But he told us that he did not find them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: It was subsequently, later on, that he told you that?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, later on he told us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know if the Muslims were locked up in Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did they go to that house of their own free will?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, they went there of their own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that Mirsad Osmancevic and his family went to Rovna. Did he leave of his own free will or not?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, he left of his own will, because Jozo Cerkez had a daughter, and Mirsad's child and -- I mean they were very, very close and they played together, and they were also --

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: He was their godfather, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, he was their godfather.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know if Drago Josipovic helped Mirsad Osmancevic to get to Rovna because of his family?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I do know Drago Josipovic was the one who took him to Rovna.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did you hear that or --

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that Drago had taken him to Rovna and even given him his vest so as to be safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But wasn't that a major risk for Drago Josipovic? Wasn't Drago Josipovic risking very much when he gave his vest to Mirsad Osmancevic, who was a member of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Of course it was a big risk, because everybody knew that Mirsad Osmancevic was a member of the army of B and H.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When Mirsad Osmancevic returned to Anto Papic's house, were Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic, your husband, Anto Bralo, and Frano Kovac, were they afraid when they saw him come back?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Of course they were, of course they were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: When Mirsad Osmancevic went to Rovna, did any other Muslim go to Rovna, if he wants to, without any problem?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Why not? They all could go wherever they wanted, but presumably they wanted to stay together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were they safe, since they knew Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, they were safe. Had they not felt safe, they wouldn't have come there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now tell us, how is it that they could be under such poor conditions, yet spend the whole day and the night at Anto Papic's house? What were those conditions? Were they hard or not?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Oh, yes, they were hard. Oh, of course, it must have been very hard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You think the conditions were very, very hard?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I think they were very, very hard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Let us not mention anything else. But was there a bathroom in Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No, there was not a bathroom, and the conditions were nothing to write home about. I mean those people shouldn't have been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But Anto Papic and Drago Josipovic, did they want to save the Muslims they had helped to reach Anto Papic's house, to get to Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes, of course, because they were there amongst us, and nobody was hurt and they were safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You said that you knew Frano and Katica Kovac. Who is Frano Kovac?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Frano Kovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where did he work?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: He worked in Novi Travnik. He was a salesperson there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But did he live in Novi Travnik or in Santici?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, he spent more time in Novi Travnik, living there, because of his work.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Do you know if Drago Josipovic's mother came to Katica Kovac's house or, rather, the house in which she lived?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Whose house did they live in?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Katica Kovac lived in her father's house. It's a rather old house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Were they building their own house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, they were building their own house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I know they were building it, but had they built it?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No. They built it only after the war. It was after the war that they finished it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: We said that the Muslims were in Anto Papic's house, but could those Muslims come to your house, had they wanted to?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Did anyone stop them?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No, nobody stopped them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But a short while ago you mentioned some of them. Did they come to visit you of their own will?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Of their own will.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they came of their own will?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Of their own will.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And do you know if the Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASESSE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you not to repeat the same questions. I mean you're asking questions you have already asked I mean at least twice. Could you be so kind as to move on to other matters? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. I am about to finish, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So I shall repeat this question. Do you know if Muslims came to Nikola Omazic's house? [realtime transcript read in error "Niko Ahmic's house"]

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (redacted) came. She came to call her son, who was living in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You mean she used the telephone?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, she used the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: To conclude, which Croats were in your house on the 16th of April, '93?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: The Croats in my house were Marija Papic and Ivica Papic, Zeljko Papic, Ljubica Filipovic and Maja Filipovic, Finka Vidovic, Simo Vidovic, Jozo Santic. I think that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I shall merely like to show an aerial photograph to the witness, and then I would end my examination with this. So will the usher please help me?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 34/4.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am warned that it is wrongly recorded. She was to answer the question whether Muslims were in Nikola Omazic's house on the 16th of April, not Niko Ahmic's house. Nikola Omazic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mrs. Bralo, could you manage? Can you find your way around this photograph? If not, you can turn it around. You can turn it around, if it will make it easier for you. Can you find Ogrjev?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I am finding my way about it. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Could you show us where Nikola Omazic's house is? Will you put a circle?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Just a moment. Nikola Omazic's, it's this house here (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Will you put number "2" to it?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now put a circle around Anto Papic's house, Anto Papic, and put number "1".

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now put a circle around Anto Bralo's house, if you know where that is, Anto Bralo. Put a "3" next to it.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I shall ask you a question. On the 16th -- can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On the 16th, did you see Drago Josipovic on several occasions that day?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Where did they move about, he and Bralo and Kovac and Anto Papic; where did --

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, they used that lane between Anto Bralo, Nikola Omazic and Anto Papic's houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So they were roughly in that place?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, in that crossroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How many times did you see them that day; could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, I saw them several times, a number of times throughout the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. So the group of houses which are a cluster of Muslim houses towards the road, will you please put circles around them and tell us who they belong to?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: This is Zenur Ramic (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Circle it and put the letter "A".

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks) Then Cazim Ramic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Put a "B" and a circle.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks) Then Naim Ahmic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Naim or Nail?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Naim.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Naim Ahmic. Put a "C".

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks) Mirsad Osmancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now "D". That is, circle and "D".

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks) And Frano Kovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. Just draw a circle and put a "Y".

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, the question. Will you tell us, from these houses, their residents came to Anto Papic's house of their own will, or were brought there on the 16th of April, 1993, did anyone get killed or wounded among those residents?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Was any of those Muslim houses set on fire? I mean Muslim houses. Were they damaged or anything?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, one house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But when?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: On the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But give us the full answer. 17th of what?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: 17th of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: March? There was no war in March. Do you mean April?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: April.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So will you please repeat it?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: 17th of April, '93.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So only one house was set on fire, and whose house was it?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: It was Cazim Ramic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And Cazim and Razim Ahmic's house, does it have windows? Could he look out of that window towards Nikola Omazic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, in all directions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That morning, did he look also out of the window of Naim Ahmic's in which he took shelter then? Could he see Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic on their way to Omazic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, he could.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now will you also draw a circle around Fahran Ahmic's house or Hasim Ahmic's? No, Hasim Ahmic's house is what you should draw a circle around, and put Roman I.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Fahran?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes. Draw a circle and put Roman I.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now draw a circle around (redacted)'s house and put a Roman II.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That's it. On the same photograph, will you draw circles around Rasim or, rather, Razim Ahmic's, Nazif's and Asim's?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: You could also put there "A", "B", "C" next to those houses; that is, Razim with "A", Nazif's with "B", and Asim's with a C"?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What about the visibility looking from (redacted)? Does she have good visibility? Does she have a good view of the road?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, the visibility is good.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: From (redacted) in the direction of Fahrudin Ahmic's house, can you see?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, you can, because it's all clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Is it all clear? Are those fields or woods?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: These are fields which are sown.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Since we're talking about the 16th of April, '93, was there any vegetation up there, were there leaves in the wood or not?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you mean it was all exposed. What does one grow in those fields?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, this is vegetables, mostly some maize, some wheat.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What month? What is the sowing time?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, end of April, early May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: On this aerial photograph, will you please draw an arrow to show the direction from Fahran Ahmic's house to Anto Papic's house? To Anto Papic's house. You can draw a line.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Yes, to the end. That's it. Now an arrow from (redacted) to Razim Ahmic's house. Also an arrow. Will you please do that?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Find (redacted)'s house.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now draw an arrow towards Razim/Asim's houses.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: (Witness marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: That's it. How far is that house away from (redacted)? What is the distance between them?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, it could be about 40 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: From Fahran Ahmic's house to the road?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: About 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: To conclude, do you know how many Muslims were killed on the 16th of April, '93, in this direction from Anto Papic's house towards the road?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Fahran Ahmic and Puscul.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: What's his name?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Excuse me. We're really trying not to interfere too much and not to raise any objections, but the last question which is asked is completely incomprehensible. What does it mean? "Do you know the number of Muslims killed in the direction of Anto Papic's house?" I simply don't understand this. Could Mr. Susak rephrase his question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Susak, could you please be so kind as to rephrase your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, let me answer straightaway to my learned friend in the Prosecution. These houses are important because one needs to see where Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic -- that is, that no Muslim was killed in their vicinity or, rather, that they were safe, and also that no Muslim homes which they protected was set on fire on the 16th of April, '93. This is an important question to show that it was the Muslim houses by the road which were damaged, and this is one of the questions which the Prosecution seems to avoid, because the military police was protecting the Busovaca-Vitez road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So, Mrs. Bralo, will you please -- and this is my last question. How far is Fahrudin Ahmic's house away from the road, what is the distance?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Twenty metres. That is how I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Let me just ask Counsel Pavkovic if there is any Defence counsel willing to ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have no questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: So I suggest that we now take a 15-minute break, and then the Prosecution will cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Terrier?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. My name is Franck Terrier. I'm one of the representatives of the Prosecution in these proceedings, and I have a few questions for you. I don't think I will take too long.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: First of all, I should like to ask you to indicate, with greater precision than you have done so far, what was your job? You said that you worked for UNPROFOR, but more specifically, who was your employer?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I worked in UNPROFOR as a cleaning lady. I cleaned the premises. If that is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Was that for the British Battalion based in Vitez that you worked for?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When did you start your job with them?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: From when, you mean? You mean in time? Or how long I worked for them?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'm asking you the date, if you can tell us; if not, the period when you worked for them.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Five days before the shooting started, before the war broke out, I started working for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And after the 16th of April, 1993, did you resume working for the British Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I did not continue working because I couldn't travel. There was a war. There was shooting. And because of the war, I was left jobless.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, I come to the 16th of April, 1993, but before that, I should like to ask you to tell us only what your personal memories are of the things that interest us and will be of interest to the Trial Chamber. So we want your personal experiences. Not what you suppose, not what you heard other people say; only the things that you, yourself, remember. Could you please tell us at what point in time, according to your personal memory, you saw Drago Josipovic on that day?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: There was gunfire, and it was twenty to 6.00, on the road between the old house of Nikola Omazic and the new house of Frano Kovac. That is where I saw him. And coming towards him was (redacted), (redacted), and three children. They stopped there on the road. They exchanged a few words. Drago and Anto Papic were together. Then they went back with (redacted) towards Anto Papic's house. They went inside, inside the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Where were you when you saw all this, all that you have just described? Where were you?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I was on the balcony of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Were you on the first floor, if there is a first floor, or were you on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: The lower level was the basement, and I was on the first level, on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you describe for us, what was the view that you had left and right from the position where you were standing? How far could you see? What houses could you see from the spot where you were standing, from that balcony?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I could see the old house of Nikola Omazic, and the concrete slab of Frano Kovac's house, and Zenur Ramic's house, and Zilka Ramic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that your house is in a kind of valley, in a kind of depression?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is, a small valley, a small depression.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And despite this depression in the ground, you still had the view that you have just told us; that is, rather a wide view?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, very wide, because the house is not so low down.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Could you tell us now how you can be certain of the time that you have indicated?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: How can I not be sure, when all these things were happening in the space of only a few minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, but my question was whether you had a clock or a watch on you or in front of you. Was there any particular reason that made you look at your watch?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I didn't look at my watch, but roughly one can tell how much time this could have taken from the moment the gunfire started to that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So to be more precise, your memory is that things went very fast, and this makes you believe that it was approximately 20 to 6.00, but you didn't look at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But you did not consult a clock or a watch; it is what you presume. Isn't that so, from your testimony?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: That was the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: When you saw Drago Josipovic in the circumstances that you have just indicated, was he carrying a weapon?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I didn't see it. I personally did not see a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did Anto Papic have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I didn't see a weapon on Anto Papic either, but it's possible he may have.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did your husband, Anto Bralo, carry a weapon?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: He did have a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What type of weapon was it?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I don't know exactly the names of those weapons, but he did have one. I think it was an old rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did your husband, Anto Bralo, wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, but an UNPROFOR uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Previously, prior to the 16th of April, 1993 -- for example, on the 20th of October, 1992, the date of the first events, the first conflict -- did you have occasion to see Drago Josipovic carrying a weapon or any parts of a uniform?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Gladly. Before the 16th of April, 1993, and specifically on the 20th of October, 1992, did you have occasion to see Drago Josipovic carrying parts of a uniform or a weapon?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: You spoke to us, madam, about Drago Josipovic's visit on the 17th of April around 9.00. If I remember well, Drago Josipovic came to have a cup of coffee in your place, and he stayed for about an hour. Do you recall, and could you tell us what you discussed? What was the atmosphere of that meeting?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: While having coffee, we discussed that particular situation; that is, the situation of the previous day and what had happened. And all of us, of course, were very sorry about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, my question may be a difficult one, but during that encounter, more than 30 refugees were gathered at Anto Papic's; several people were killed in the vicinity of your house, in your area. In view of those facts, I was wondering, what was the atmosphere, what you said; do you remember Drago Josipovic saying anything in connection with all that?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: We didn't even know how many people had been killed, nor what had happened, because we were all round about there, myself, my husband, and my neighbours, among whom was Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But, madam, you know that several of your neighbours were killed. You met (redacted); you just told us about it. You knew that several Muslim houses in your area had been torched.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness said that not a single Muslim house was set on fire on the 16th, nor was any one of their Muslim neighbours killed on that day. So I object to this question, because no Muslim was killed in their immediate neighbourhood on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Let things be clear. I'm talking about your area; that is, the triangle going from Anto Papic's house to Drago Josipovic's house to Ramiz Ahmic's house. You can see that, you can imagine that triangle, more or less?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: And you're telling us that on the 16th of April, in this area that I've just described, not a single Muslim house was destroyed or burnt and that not a single Muslim was killed?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I did not say that. One house was burnt down: Cazim Ramiz's. And nearer to the road, those two persons were killed. One house is some 50 to 60 metres away, and the other about 20 metres away. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I should like to show the witness Exhibit 208. It is under seal, an exhibit under seal, but with the agreement of the technical booth, we need not reproduce it on the monitors. We need not reproduce the elements that are protected from the public. So Exhibit Number 208, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Madam, I should like to draw your attention to this area appearing between the main road, the Vitez-to-Busovaca road, the two roads that branch off, and the wood. It is at the bottom of the page, marked by Anto Papic's house, to the right by the group of houses around Drago Josipovic and his family, and at the other side by the house of Ramiz Ahmic. You told us that from your balcony, you had a good view of Nikola Omazic's house; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: If you had a good view towards Nikola Omazic's house -- and the ground is flat; we have been able to see this -- what prevents you from seeing the (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: What prevented me was the fact that their houses are closer to the road, and my house is closer to Nikola Omazic's, as can be seen here on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that clearly. But the ground is absolutely flat. It is a low land, and we were able to note by consulting photographs and seeing videotapes that that is so. So my question is: As you were able to see Nikola Omazic's house from your balcony, and as it's still flat all the way to the road, I don't see why you couldn't see (redacted), for instance.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: If I had gone into the yard, slightly above the house, then I may have been able to see it. But my house is on a slope, and about half a metre, the height of the hedge, that is how far it is below the level. If I had climbed up to the meadow, I could have been able to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But I'm asking you to tell us what was your view from your balcony, and show us the houses you could see where you were standing when you saw Drago Josipovic, which of the houses that you saw from your balcony. Could you pinpoint them for us?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: This is my house (indicating). I could see Ramic Zenur, Ramic Cazim, Frano Kovac, and Nikola Omazic's houses (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: So from your balcony you saw particularly Nikola Omazic's house, in which Mr. Bukovac was staying at the time, but you couldn't see anything beyond that?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Of course I couldn't see what was behind the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I also draw your attention, madam, to the fact that in the area we are referring to, ten persons were killed; and more specifically, according to our information, eight persons were killed on the 16th of April and two others on the 17th of April. You have no information about that?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: None. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: All the houses, the Muslim houses between Nikola Omazic's house and the road, were torched on the 16th of April. You didn't see that?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Between Nikola Omazic's -- could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: All the houses, Muslim houses, situated between Nikola Omazic's house and the road were set on fire on the 16th of April, 1993. And you didn't see it?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: One house was set on fire. One house was set on fire. Cazim Ramic's house, on the 17th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I'm referring, madam, to seven houses; seven.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: In my street, only one house. And closer to the road, Fahran Ahmic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Very well. I should like to go back to the question that I wanted to ask you regarding this encounter on the 17th of April, in the morning, when at least a significant number of refugees were in Anto Papic's house, as you know and you told us. I want to ask you whether you remember what Drago Josipovic may have said that morning, if you remember, of course. If you don't remember, tell us so, if you have no information to tell us on that subject.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: What Drago said to whom? To whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did he tell you anything on the 17th of April in the morning as to what had happened, what he thought, what he intended to do, how he felt? If he said nothing, he said nothing.

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: While he was in my house, we discussed the situation as it had occurred, and that he was sorry, and we were all sorry. He didn't say anything more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you speak about the refugees in Anto Papic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, of course we did. We spoke about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: What did he say about them?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: He said that the conditions there were not appropriate; that it wasn't very comfortable for them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Do you know where Drago Josipovic's family was on the 16th and 17th of April?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Did you ask Drago Josipovic, or did he give you any information on the subject at all?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I think they were in Rovna, because his wife's parents are there, and they were certainly there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: But you didn't see them leave for Rovna? You, personally?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Mr. Susak?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mrs. Bralo, your house, is your house at a lower level of ground?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And does your lane go through the field, or does it go around it because of the slight elevation beyond your house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: It goes around.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And the lower part of your house, or as you called it, the basement, is it dug into the ground?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, half of the house is a basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So, practically, it is dug into the ground, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes, it is dug into the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And you cannot say that the upper part of your house is an upper floor; it is the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And when you look from the house in the direction of the road, is there a steep slope or not?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No, it isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And when you look at your house, is it in a small depression or not?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And when you come out on the hill which is 30 metres from your house, could you see the whole area down to Musafer Puscul's house and Fahran Ahmic's house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, if I come out from my house and go up, then I have a very good view. I can see all the houses to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And let me conclude: The Prosecution asked you what you could see from the terrace of your house, and you said that from the terrace you saw Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic when they met, when they caught up with (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Now, before that, before you went back to your house, whom did you meet in front of your house? Rather, who came to your house?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Frano Kovac and Kata Kovac, with their son.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And where did you meet them?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: In front of the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Your house, you mean?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And from that position -- that is, when you were in front of your house -- could you see Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic standing at the crossroad?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And when you went back into the house, then, from the terrace, you said you saw Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic meeting up with (redacted) and her family somewhere near Nikola Omazic's house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And now my last question. You were asked by the Prosecutor, and you said that Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic met (redacted) sometime around 5.40; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: And when you saw Drago Josipovic and Anto Papic at the crossroad, what time was it then? Was it before or after?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: It was before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So what time could it have been?

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: Well, it could have been about 20 to 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: But you say it was 20 to --

utterances.speaker: FINKA BRALO
utterances.text: No, it could have been 25 to 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: So you would say 25 to 5.00, in your judgement? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We don't have any questions for you, Mrs. Bralo. Thank you for testifying. You may now be released. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: And we will adjourn now until -- I imagine Mr. Bralo is not available, so we adjourn now?

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: Mr. President, you are quite right. He is the only witness we have for this week, and he will be here tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
